findings.evidence: Page 60: "Table 3-2 — MoE model parameter arithmetic (worked example, not reference). The active fraction for top-2-of-8 routing is ~24–27% of total, not single-digit." Row: "Total parameters (across 8 experts) | ~47B | ~5.7B per expert × 8 = 45.6B + ~1.4B always-on (attention/shared + embeddings) = 47B [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]". Row: "Active parameters per token (top-2 routing) | ~12.8B | 2 × 5.7B routed experts + ~1.4B always-on attention/shared = 12.8B (~27% of the ~47B total; ~24% counting expert-FFN mass alone) [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]". Page 60 prose: "Its published model card gives 46.7B total and 12.9B active parameters per token [1P][FACT]. The numbers below use the component-derived ~47B / ~12.8B (2 × 5.7B routed experts + ~1.4B always-on); the component sum sits 0.1B below the model card's 12.9B active count, and the numbers carry the illustrative flag."
findings.issue: The 12.8B / 47B = 27.23% derivation checks, and the 5.5× vs 3.7× baseline distinction is stated correctly. The defect is provenance: the table presents '~5.7B per expert' and '~1.4B always-on' — which are the published Mixtral-8x7B figures (46.7B total = 8 × 6.9B, of which 46.7 − 8×5.7 = ~1.1B attention/shared/embeddings; the published figure is ~6.9B per expert with ~12.9B active = 2×6.9 + 3.3) — as [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED], while the very same paragraph's first sentence cites the model card as [1P][FACT] for 46.7B/12.9B. Two different component decompositions of the same named model card are presented, and the book never explains why it declines to use the card's own per-expert figure (6.9B) in favor of 5.7B. The result is that a reader who checks the model card finds neither 5.7B nor ~1.4B in it, and the book's numbers are labelled only as 'illustrative' — never as a derivation from the cited card.
findings.fix_instruction: Either use the model card's own decomposition (8 experts × 6.9B, active 12.9B = 2×6.9B + always-on) tagged [1P][FACT]/[1P][DERIVED], or add one sentence stating why 5.7B and 1.4B were used instead of the card's figures and what source they come from, so the reader can resolve the divergence.

findings.evidence: Page 63: "The boxed rule — two distinct accounting lines. Keep two numbers separate and never blur them: 1. total parameters → weight residency. The resident weights (all experts, for MoE) are what the GPUs must hold. For a 70B dense model this is ~140 GB FP16; for a ~47B MoE this is ~94 GB (full expert set) unless experts are explicitly offloaded. 2. active parameters/token → approximate compute per token." Page 70 (mini-case): "Active-compute memory yes — only ~12.8B of the ~47B total is active per token, so ~25.6 GB of active weight footprint is read per batch-1 decode token vs. 140 GB for a dense 70B."
findings.issue: The mini-case on p. 70 answers the question 'If we go MoE, can we cut our GPU memory budget?' with 'Active-compute memory yes', which conflates the two lines the same chapter's boxed rule (p. 63) forbids blurring: ~25.6 GB is a per-token *read* volume, not a memory budget, and p. 63's own line 2 says the active count is 'not a memory-freeing lever unless offloading is in play'. The answer 'Active-compute memory yes' reads as a memory-budget saving that the chapter explicitly says is not one, immediately before stating 'Resident memory yes as well, for this challenger'. A reader scanning the mini-case takeaway will record two 'yes' answers to a memory question where only one ('resident memory, and only because 47B < 70B') is correct.
findings.fix_instruction: Rewrite the mini-case's answer so the first line reads 'Active-compute *traffic* yes (a per-token read volume, not a memory budget)' — matching the boxed rule on p. 63 — and keep 'Resident memory yes' as the only memory-budget answer.

findings.evidence: Page 48: "Weight residency (Ch 7's floor): the active-weight working set for Qwen is ~6 × 10⁹ params × 2 bytes/param = ~12 GB read per batch-1 decode token — ~12× less per-token weight traffic than the canonical dense 70B (140 GB → 12 GB), and ~1/21 of Qwen's own total weight footprint (~250 GB → 12 GB)."
findings.issue: The phrase 'Weight residency (Ch 7's floor)' is followed immediately by a quantity that is a read volume, not a residency floor — the same confusion the chapter's boxed rule (p. 63) was written to prevent. The paragraph's own next sentence says 'this is a compute/bandwidth statement, not a residency one: the total weights dominate the memory ceiling, ~125 × 10⁹ params × 2 bytes/param ≈ 250 GB'. So the subsection labels a non-residency number as 'weight residency'. Separately, the arithmetic is loose: 140 GB → 12 GB is ~11.7×, printed as '~12×' (acceptable), but '~1/21 of Qwen's own total weight footprint (~250 GB → 12 GB)' is computed as 250/12 ≈ 20.8 — '~1/21' is a rounding of 1/20.8, which is fine, though the mixed fraction-and-arrow notation is imprecise.
findings.fix_instruction: Rename the bullet heading from 'Weight residency (Ch 7's floor)' to 'Active-weight read traffic per batch-1 decode token' and move the residency figure (~250 GB total) into that bullet's first sentence so the label and the quantity match.

findings.evidence: Page 66: "Qwen3.8-Flash-Next. The model card [1P][FACT] (source: HF Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) is the Qwen4-architecture preview: 125B total / 6B active (plus a separate 51B of offloadable N-gram embedding parameters), 512 MoE experts (10 routed + 1 shared per token), and hybrid attention — Gated DeltaNet (GDN) on three of every four layers plus Qwen Sparse Attention (QSA) on the fourth." Page 68, Fig 3.3 caption: "Wan2.2 A14B selects experts as the denoising schedule progresses: two resident checkpoints supply the high- and low-noise stages; only the selected expert runs in a branch evaluation ... Scope: official rounded counts (about 27B total, about 14B active), not an inferred per-expert split".
findings.issue: Two first-party facts are asserted with the tag [1P][FACT] but with only a bare 'HF Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next' pointer (no commit/revision/date), while every other post-cutoff inspection in the book carries a pinned revision and retrieval date (e.g. p. 40: 'Wan2.2 source, pinned revision 1ea34ff, retrieved 2026-10-28'). The Preface (p. 18) states: 'Primary sources ... were accessed as of the build date and each is cited with a stable identifier in the References chapter'. A bare Hugging Face model-card URL is a stable identifier, so this is defensible — but the same page's 'plus a separate 51B of offloadable N-gram embedding parameters' and the '512 MoE experts (10 routed + 1 shared per token)' figures are unusually specific and are presented as [1P][FACT] without any access date or A.10 pointer, unlike the equivalent Qwen claim in Table 7-3 (p. 166) which carries 'accessed 2026-08-30; A.10'.
findings.fix_instruction: Give the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next citation the same form as Table 7-3's ('model card HF Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, accessed 2026-08-30; A.10') wherever it is used in Ch. 3, so the same first-party figure has one consistent citation form across chapters.

findings.evidence: Page 55: "• Dense models activate all parameters for every token. A 70B dense model reads all 70B weights (or close to it) on every batch-1 decode step — the weight-read-per-token figures in this chapter are all batch-1 single-token decode values, amortized across the batch at batch size B — because every layer's full hidden dimension participates in every attention and feed-forward computation. The parameter count on the model card is the inference cost count."
findings.issue: The parenthetical 'amortized across the batch at batch size B' is placed inside the sentence that defines the batch-1 figures, and is ambiguous: it can be read as saying these batch-1 numbers are themselves amortized (they are not) or as a forward reference to Ch. 2's batch-amortization discussion. It also conflicts with the book's own repeated correction that the batch-1-equivalent read is an idealization, not physical traffic (p. 28: 'This is the footprint that results from reading every parameter once per decode step in a dense model with no reuse, not a claim about physical HBM traffic in a real engine'; p. 30: 'a batch-1-equivalent idealized weight-streaming read (one request's full weight pass), not a measured bytes-physically-read figure'). Ch. 3 states it without that qualifier.
findings.fix_instruction: Move the batch-amortization clause out of the batch-1 definition sentence into its own sentence, and add the book's standard qualifier that the batch-1 figure is an idealized weight-streaming read rather than measured physical traffic.

findings.evidence: Page 62: "MoE sparsity = compute sparsity (fewer FLOPs per token). MoE sparsity ≠ memory sparsity (KV cache still grows linearly with context length, exactly as a dense model's does at the same attention shape). Only changing the attention mechanism itself (e.g., hybrid/linear attention) can stop the cache from growing — KV offload changes where the cache resides, not how fast it grows. MLA-style latent attention does not stop the growth: it cuts the bytes/token constant (~50–60× for DeepSeek-class geometry: 32,768/576 ≈ 57× per Ch 1, DeepSeek-V2 MLA report, arXiv:2405.04434 [1P][DERIVED])"
findings.issue: Two issues. (a) The '~50–60×' band is repeated here and tagged [1P][DERIVED] — the same untagged editorial band first noted on p. 26, so the recurrence sweep confirms it: the band appears on p. 26 (inside the taxonomy table) and p. 62 and p. 71 (Fig 3.4's text says 'the bytes per token follow each model's own attention shape') with no source in any occurrence. (b) The claim 'Only changing the attention mechanism itself (e.g., hybrid/linear attention) can stop the cache from growing' conflicts with Ch. 7's own account of hybrid models: the Qwen3.8-27B configuration (p. 153) has 16 full-attention layers whose KV still grows, with the other 48 layers holding fixed-size recurrent state — so a hybrid model does NOT stop the cache from growing, it reduces the fraction of layers that grow. Ch. 7's own Fig 7.2 shows exactly this ('Full-attention layers: growing key/value (KV) history').
findings.fix_instruction: Correct the categorical claim to 'only changing the attention mechanism can stop the cache from growing' → 'can reduce the growth rate (fewer growing layers) or, with no full-attention layers, stop it', consistent with Ch. 7's hybrid Qwen3.8-27B treatment; and either source the '~50–60× band' or drop it to the single sourced ratio (32,768/576 ≈ 57×).

findings.evidence: Page 66: "Why the rest of this chapter's canonical stays a dense full-MHA model. ... Because a dense model with full multi-head attention gives the cleanest single-constant KV formula (2 × layers × hidden × bytes) and the largest KV footprint — the conservative worst case an architect should always size against first." Page 92 (Ch. 4 Table 4-2): "Attention architecture | full-MHA reference model (K/V width = hidden_dim) | [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] (a real 70B may use GQA, ~8x less KV; Ch 7)". Page 131 (Ch. 7): "Attention-family sensitivity note. The ~2.62 MB/token (2.5 MiB) figure is the full-MHA (multi-head attention) upper bound."
findings.issue: The book is internally consistent on the full-MHA-as-upper-bound point, and Table 4-2 flags it. The defect is that the canonical 70B figure is described on p. 66 as 'a conservative worst case an architect should always size against first' and on p. 92 as 'a real 70B may use GQA, ~8x less KV', yet Ch. 5 §5.3.2 (p. 118) states the canonical model's KV cost twice — once at the teaching bound (~24.1 GB) and once for a named checkpoint (Llama-2/3 70B GQA-8, ~3.0 GB) — and then Ch. 5's own recommendation (p. 126) and Ch. 7's GQA note (p. 131: 'the fleet-sizing arithmetic of Chapter 17 changes accordingly (many more concurrent requests fit for KV)') imply the fleet numbers (17 slots, 6/21 hosts, all Ch. 16–17 cost figures) are stated on the conservative bound. Nowhere in Ch. 16/17's own text (as previewed in the front matter's figure list: '16.1 Takeaway: the frozen 21-host self-host line . . . 310'; '17.1 Sizing a fleet by burst peak, headroom and failover . . . 314') is the GQA relaxation priced. So the book's headline fleet and cost numbers are all bound-based, with the relaxation noted but never quantified.
findings.fix_instruction: In Ch. 16 and Ch. 17, add one explicit paragraph stating the effect of the GQA-8 relaxation on the per-host slot count, host count and monthly cost (e.g. 436 ÷ 3.1 GB ≈ 140 slots per host, and the resulting host counts and $ figures), so the reader can see how much the headline fleet numbers depend on the deliberately conservative teaching geometry.

findings.evidence: Page 66: "Stepping through this book's own arithmetic: • Weight residency (Ch 7's floor): the active-weight working set for Qwen is ~6 × 10⁹ params × 2 bytes/param = ~12 GB read per batch-1 decode token ... • KV cache (Ch 7/8): the canonical 2 × layers × hidden × bytes KV formula is the full-MHA bound. Qwen's hybrid attention attacks the KV constant at the mechanism level ... So per-token KV no longer follows the dense formula, and no KV metric for this model is stated anywhere in this book."
findings.issue: The book states 'no KV metric for this model is stated anywhere in this book' and then says 'Chapter 7 works a configuration-backed version of exactly this two-term budget — Qwen3.8-27B's 16 full-attention layers priced separately from its 48 Gated DeltaNet layers — into its own history-state arithmetic'. But Ch. 7 §7.3.2 (p. 153) does state KV metrics for Qwen3.8-27B: '2 × 16 × 4 × 256 × 2 = 65,536 bytes per cached token. At 262,144 cached tokens, this component occupies 16 GiB. ... At 131,072 tokens the same component is 8 GiB.' These are KV metrics for a Qwen model in this book, which contradicts 'no KV metric for this model is stated anywhere in this book' — unless 'this model' means specifically Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (a different model from Qwen3.8-27B). The sentence is ambiguous on a load-bearing point and reads as a contradiction on a fast reader.
findings.fix_instruction: Rewrite as 'no KV metric for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next is stated anywhere in this book' (naming the specific checkpoint) and, since Qwen3.8-27B is a different model in the same family, add a parenthetical 'the related Qwen3.8-27B is priced separately in Ch. 7 §7.3.2' so the reader does not read the sentence as contradicting Ch. 7.

findings.evidence: Page 63: "Key takeaway: MoE provides compute sparsity (far fewer FLOPs per token because a fraction of experts is active), not automatic weight-residency sparsity — the full expert set normally remains resident unless it is explicitly offloaded or sharded in a way that changes residency." Page 63 Fig 3.4 text: "MoE total resident ≈ 94 GB = 91 GB experts + 3 GB always-on". Recompute: 8 × 5.7B = 45.6B params × 2 B = 91.2 GB ✓; always-on 1.4B × 2 = 2.8 GB ≈ 3 GB ✓; total 94.0 GB ✓.
findings.issue: The arithmetic checks. The defect is a consistency one with Ch. 3's own Table 3-2/3-3: those tables state '~47B' total = '45.6B + ~1.4B always-on' and the active count '~12.8B = 11.4B routed + 1.4B always-on'. Fig 3.4 states 'active experts ≈ 23 GB resident (2 × 11.4)' and 'per token: top-2 = 11.4B ... + 1.4B always-on = 12.8B → 25.6 GB'. 2 × 11.4 GB = 22.8 ≈ 23 ✓ and 11.4 + 2.8 = 14.2 GB, but Fig 3.4 says the per-token read is '25.6 GB' (= 12.8B × 2) — consistent. However, Fig 3.4's 'inactive experts ≈ 68 GB (6 × 11.4)' → 6 × 11.4 = 68.4 ✓, and 91.2 + 68.4 would double-count if the 68 GB were part of the 91 GB; the figure shows 'active experts ≈ 23 GB' and 'inactive experts ≈ 68 GB' as separate boxes within the 'MoE total resident ≈ 94 GB = 91 GB experts + 3 GB always-on' label, and 23 + 68 = 91 ✓. The arithmetic is coherent. The remaining defect is that '1 expert = 5.7B params ≈ 11.4 GB (FP16)' is stated in the figure with no provenance, while the text on p. 61 flags the whole column as [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] — the figure's own labels carry no tag, so the figure can be lifted as a set of facts.
findings.fix_instruction: Add a provenance line to Fig 3.4's caption (or to each label) carrying the [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] status of the MoE column, so the figure's numbers cannot be read as vendor specifications.
